children: Shares of online fast-fashion retailer Shein
dropped more than 10% in gray-market trading on Monday ahead of its Hong Kong Stock Exchange debut on Tuesday.
The company raised $1.7 billion at HK$48.56 a share, valuing the company at about $26.5 billion, sources told Reuters.
Shein's gray-market trading in major Hong Kong brokers Futu Securities, Bright Smart and Phillip Securities, all dropped more than 10% within a few minutes after trading began.
Gray market prices are quoted by brokerages ahead of a security being officially traded on an exchange.
